name: Portugal
dek: Lisbon's Geofísico fiche for 1991–2020. IPMA marks the series hybrid. It is not in the NCEI submission.
paragraphs: Portugal has no folder in the NOAA NCEI Region VI collection, version 6.6. The table is IPMA's 1991–2020 fiche for Lisboa / Instituto Geofísico, station 535, at 77.0 m, 38.7191°N, 9.1497°W, version 1.0 of 2024. The fiche says the series is hybrid: observed stations plus WRF-modelled values. That caveat is the file's, and the numbers are still the ones IPMA published for this station. They are not a pure observed normal, and they are not a national average.

Gago Coutinho and Tapada are other Lisbon fiches, also marked hybrid, and were not averaged with Geofísico. Madeira and the Azores are other time zones. The mainland plug, the road rule, and the Visit Portugal tipping note are what the city sheet repeats.

climate.caption: Reference station: Lisboa / Instituto Geofísico, IPMA 535. A hybrid series, not a national average, and not in the NCEI submission.
climate.note: IPMA normal climatológica 1991–2020, Lisboa / Instituto Geofísico, station 535, version 1.0 of 2024. The fiche labels the series hybrid. The legend says the series is observed data from classical and automatic stations plus values modelled with WRF at local scale. Portugal has no folder in the NOAA NCEI Region VI 1991–2020 collection, version 6.6. Gago Coutinho and Tapada are separate Lisbon fiches, also marked hybrid, and were not averaged with this one.

plugs.label: Plugs and voltage
plugs.value: Type C and F, 230 V, 50 Hz
plugs.detail: The IEC world-plugs list, in the copy archived on 16 August 2026, shows Portugal at the voltage, frequency, and plug types in the figure. A direct download of the live page on 15 November 2026 did not return the list. The archive is the copy that was read.

driving.label: Driving side
driving.detail: Article 13 of the Código da Estrada, in the consolidated text of Decree-Law 114/94 kept by the Lisbon public prosecutor's office, says the driving position is on the right side of the carriageway, keeping enough distance from the verges or pavements to avoid accidents. The left side may be used when needed to overtake or to change direction. Where two or more lanes run in the same direction, traffic uses the rightmost lane, and may use another if there is no room in that one, or to overtake or change direction.

tipping.label: Tipping
tipping.detail: Visit Portugal's practical-information page says restaurant service is included in the bill, and that it is usual to leave a tip of about 5 to 10 percent of the price of the meal. The same page says a taxi tip is voluntary and that about 5 to 10 percent, or rounding up, is usual. The print carries a 2013 Turismo de Portugal copyright line. The percentages are that page's, not a newer regulation we opened.

water.label: Tap water
water.detail: CDC's traveler page for Portugal, last reviewed 25 August 2026, does not say whether tap water is safe or unsafe. It says food and water standards around the world vary based on the destination, that standards may also differ within a country, and that risk may change depending on the activity. It points readers to CDC's food and water precautions. This page does not turn that into medical advice.

currency.label: Currency
currency.detail: ISO 4217 lists the currency name Euro and the code EUR for Portugal.

timeZone.label: Time zone
timeZone.detail: IANA's zone1970.tab and zone.tab each give Portugal three rows. Europe/Lisbon is commented Portugal (mainland). Atlantic/Madeira is commented Madeira Islands. Atlantic/Azores is commented Azores. Lisbon is the mainland row. This sheet does not put Madeira or the Azores on Europe/Lisbon.
